object_context: Child of NS-B1a. Let (v,q) be a non-trivial mild bounded ancient 3D incompressible Navier-Stokes solution on R^3 x (-infinity,0) with finite Albritton-Barker Type-I quantity I=sup_Q(A+C+D+E). Determine whether the standard suitable-solution local-energy inequality, with parabolic cutoffs on dynamically realized dyadic scales, supplies a scale-decaying, telescoping, monotone, no-recrossing, or otherwise finite total charge that can terminate infinite scale descent. The immediate discriminator is absolute scale accounting only; no theorem candidate is authorized.
structural_coordinates: Navier-Stokes scaling v_lambda(x,t)=lambda v(lambda x,lambda^2 t), q_lambda=lambda^2 q(lambda x,lambda^2 t)
Albritton-Barker scale-invariant A,C,D,E on parabolic cylinders
local energy inequality with cutoff derivatives |dt phi|+|Delta phi|=O(R^-2), |grad phi|=O(R^-1)
natural localized kinetic-energy scale is R, so shell bookkeeping must be normalized by R
velocity cutoff term, cubic transport, pressure-velocity flux, dissipation and endpoint energy must be typed separately
pressure is normalized modulo a time-dependent spatial constant and must retain local Calderon-Zygmund plus harmonic/far-field structure
absolute shell bounds are distinct from signed/telescoping increments
nested critical core quantities are distinct from disjoint physical annuli
translation/dilation noncompactness and moving centers can leak a profile from any fixed shell
a Type-I singularity is represented by a non-trivial mild bounded ancient finite-I limit, not by a terminal smallest physical scale
far-field decay/global L3 is not inherited from local compactness alone
Type-II blow-up remains outside this atom
equivalent_formulations: Scale-currency form: identify a nonnegative or signed quantity whose total cost over every dynamically realized infinite dyadic descent is finite and whose per-descent effect is nontrivial.
Negative discriminator: after division by R, every canonical absolute term in the cutoff local-energy inequality is merely O(A+C+D^(2/3)C^(1/3)) and hence O(I), with no positive power of R.
Increment form: if absolute summation fails, prove a bounded-below functional Phi with a source-valid strict decrement or no-recrossing property across each certified descendant.

Rigidity form: use the resulting scale coordinate to show every non-trivial mild bounded ancient solution with finite I is impossible, or instead derive a backward sequence with bounded global L3 and invoke Albritton-Barker Theorem 1.2.
solved_analogues: Albritton-Barker Theorem 1.2: a mild ancient Navier-Stokes solution uniformly bounded in global L3 along times t_k->-infinity is zero.

Classical epsilon-regularity/persistence-of-singularities: sufficiently small scale-invariant velocity-pressure packets yield regularity; strong L3_loc compactness preserves singularity information under the required hypotheses.
near_solved_analogues: Albritton-Barker Theorem 1.1 identifies Type-I singularities with non-trivial mild bounded ancient solutions with finite I, but does not classify all such ancient solutions.

Bradshaw-Tsai construct discretely self-similar suitable weak/local-energy solutions in forward settings, showing the local-energy inequality is structurally compatible with exact scale recurrence; this is a hostile structural calibration, not an ancient blow-up example.

Lei-Yang-Yuan prove a backward-uniqueness result for bounded mild whole-space solutions with prescribed final data using weighted estimates, but finite I alone does not provide the terminal/far-field hypotheses needed to close NS-B1a1.

method_transfers.source_context: Suitable weak-solution local energy inequality and Albritton-Barker Type-I quantities
method_transfers.method: Apply a parabolic cutoff phi_R, normalize the energy inequality by R, and compute the exact homogeneity of every absolute contribution before proposing any multiscale sum.
shared_structure: same A,C,D,E quantities used to define finite Type I
same local-energy inequality available on compact subcylinders
required_assumptions: suitable/local-energy formulation on the cutoff cylinder
pressure in L^(3/2)_loc modulo a spatial constant at each time
standard cutoff derivative bounds at scale R
disanalogies: one-scale boundedness is not a finite budget over infinitely many scales
absolute values discard any cancellation that could support telescoping
annular support does not make scale-invariant normalized terms summable
method_transfers.repair_question: After the absolute O(1)-per-scale accounting is exhausted, is there a signed increment, monotone quantity, or no-recrossing theorem whose finite budget survives Navier-Stokes scaling?
source_anchors: Albritton-Barker arXiv:1811.00502, definitions (1.1)-(1.5), Definition 2.1 and Lemma 2.2

method_transfers.method: Rescale around a Type-I singularity, use uniform critical local bounds and suitable-solution compactness to extract an ancient limit, and demand strong local convergence sufficient to preserve non-triviality.
shared_structure: translation and dilation are noncompact symmetries
blow-up rescaling preserves the critical A,C,D,E quantities
rigidity is applied to an ancient limiting object
required_assumptions: uniform local L3 velocity and L^(3/2) pressure control on compact rescaled cylinders
strong L3_loc subsequential convergence of velocity
pressure normalization/decomposition and weak L^(3/2)_loc compactness
persistence of singularities or an equivalent non-triviality mechanism
disanalogies: local compactness does not control the far field
weak pressure convergence does not itself transport a global pressure normalization
moving-center descendants can leak outside a fixed annular coordinate
method_transfers.repair_question: What additional tightness/almost-periodicity theorem prevents profile leakage and binds every dynamically realized descendant to one compact scale coordinate?

method_transfers.method: Once a terminal-time or backward-sequence global hypothesis is genuinely produced, invoke a source-valid rigidity theorem rather than treating unique continuation as an automatic consequence of finite I.
shared_structure: rigidity is a possible final closure after compactness
required_assumptions: the exact global final-data/decay or L3-sequence hypothesis of the selected theorem
coefficient/regularity class required by the unique-continuation estimate
a justified far-field condition after rescaling

a local-energy shell estimate does not imply final-time vorticity vanishing
backward uniqueness cannot repair profile leakage before its hypotheses are established
method_transfers.repair_question: Can a scale increment or compactness theorem actually manufacture the terminal/global hypothesis needed by a published Liouville or backward-uniqueness theorem?

explicit_disanalogies: Forward DSS suitable weak solutions are only hostile scale-recurrence controls; they are not evidence for ancient Type-I singular solutions.
A disjoint annulus decomposition of an unnormalized finite-energy density is not the same as a summable scale-invariant charge after division by R.
A lower bound on a nested critical core packet does not imply a lower bound on each annular increment.
Pressure far-field summability from NS-B1a-C001 prunes only raw instantaneous absolute pressure accumulation; it does not prune time-integrated or signed pressure work.
No smallest dyadic singular scale may be assumed.
Local depletion/vorticity geometry cannot be promoted to global tail control without an explicit propagation or compactness theorem.
Success here would eliminate only the registered Type-I ancient branch, not Type-II blow-up or the Clay root.

cross_domain_analogies.source_situation: A process may perform infinitely many individually bounded-cost operations unless each operation consumes a strict decrement of a bounded-below potential or is charged injectively to a finite resource.
common_abstraction: uniform O(1) per step is not a termination proof
finite total budget requires telescoping, disjoint charging, or no-recrossing
the charging map must be injective enough to prevent reuse of the same resource
source_to_target_mapping: operation -> one dynamically realized scale descent R to theta R
absolute step cost -> normalized local-energy cutoff terms
bounded-below potential -> candidate Navier-Stokes monotone/increment functional
resource reuse -> nested core energy being counted at every scale
shared_constraints: infinitely many scale steps are a priori possible
critical normalization makes one-step bounds scale neutral
termination requires more than uniform boundedness
disanalogies: Navier-Stokes local energy is a signed nonlinear balance rather than a discrete algorithm
no bounded-below monotone potential is currently known in this setting
pressure and moving centers make the charging map nonlocal
cross_domain_analogies.proposed_principle: Reject absolute O(1)-per-scale bookkeeping as a terminal currency; search only for a proved decrement, injective annular renewal, or no-recrossing coordinate.
cross_domain_analogies.validation_obligation: Derive the coordinate from Navier-Stokes for every certified Type-I descendant and prove its total variation/budget is finite without assuming the desired global critical norm.
cross_domain_analogies.provenance_note: Proposal-only structural analogy; it carries no PDE theorem authority.

analogy_scan_notes: The retained potential-method analogy has a precise termination mapping. Cascade imagery and generic turbulence analogies were rejected because they do not supply a finite-budget theorem.
